product_from_film: Eureka is presented as a cargo aircraft that can take off and land on water.
explains_well: Cargo loading, underwater foils and airborne views link the aircraft to a transport purpose.
unclear: The film does not establish which views show a built aircraft or validate the performance figures.
scenario: Load cargo into a water-capable aircraft, take off and operate it as a fleet.
product_clear_basis: Cargo enters the body at 26–27s; the 30–31s underwater view explicitly labels water takeoff and landing.

scenes.action: Ships at sea, historical-looking ship images and a technical drawing accompany short progress statements. Container ships remain the recurring object.
scenes.design: Monochrome and muted footage, small central white text, some rounded frames.
scenes.purpose: Establish established shipping as the baseline.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–14s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Cloud and tail details introduce a dark aircraft. A top-down ocean view and drawing precede full rear views skimming above water at sunset.
scenes.design: Sleek dark surfaces, ocean reflections and warm sky.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 14–26s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A suspended cargo box sits over and then inside a top opening; body views follow. Underwater foils and blue flow-like visualization appear.
scenes.design: Woven-looking shell, metallic cargo box, teal water and blue streamlines.
scenes.purpose: Explain cargo capacity and water operation visually.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 26–35s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Side views show the aircraft near water, then an underside view and cloud flight. Text describes retracting foils and design performance; airflow views return.
scenes.design: Clean side silhouette and blue flow diagram; small performance text.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 35–44s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Multiple aircraft sit on water, then appear above clouds beside cost claims. A blue-lit hangar shows side and front aircraft views.
scenes.design: Sunset fleet, cloud backdrop and dark blue hangar.
scenes.purpose: Present fleet operation and material identity.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 44–55s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The front silhouette sits under a bright overhead rectangle; Eureka appears, then Break the surface and the Aspera Industries mark.
scenes.design: Black ending with restrained white text.
scenes.purpose: Name the aircraft and close the water/flight theme.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 55–60s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: Shipping baseline leads to aircraft reveal, cargo/foil details, flight claims and fleet/brand ending.
Black at 0s becomes a monochrome ship at 1–2s; the first visible subject is shipping, not the aircraft.
Cargo logistics is clear once the box and water-operation label appear at 26–31s. Buyers or operators are not explicitly named.
Aircraft positions, view angles and cargo-box height change across samples. Exact takeoff motion, camera paths and easing remain unresolved.
Technical drawings and airflow-like images interrupt scenic views to imply engineering explanation. The transitions themselves are not resolved.
Ocean light, dark woven-looking material and blue streamlines make the design feel physical and technical. Material composition is a claim, not verified by appearance.
Most specifications are small lower text while the aircraft fills the frame. The product name is delayed until 56s.
Voice delivery is unverified.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Ships, aircraft, technical drawings and flow-like graphics appear. Actual filming, render provenance and prototype status are unknown.

categories.finding: Cargo loading and foils support silent understanding of purpose. Economics and operating claims depend on small text.
The cargo opening is a clear central focus. Scenic aircraft views dominate over their small specification labels.
The opening spends 14s on ships. Several engineering and cost claims arrive in the second half with limited readable proof.
categories.experiment: Start with cargo loading and give each key specification one clean diagram.

categories.finding: The shipping-progress setup is answered by a water-capable aircraft. Break the surface neatly returns to the physical setting.
Sunset flight and fleet imagery suggest scale and possibility; this is intended emotion inferred from visuals.
The dark aircraft silhouette and ocean remain consistent from reveal through fleet. The cargo box adds a traceable functional object.
Cargo loading and foil positions are shown as presentation imagery. Flight readiness, capacity, range, cost and autonomy are not independently checked.
The water/foil/cargo combination and dark aircraft geometry are specific. Generic progress montage is less tied to this product.
Loading and foil views explain useful functions. More ship history could be removed to show one complete cargo journey.
For Tin feature explanation, pair each attractive overview with a close view of the specific mechanism and one plain label.
categories.experiment: Show a campaign workflow overview, then the exact input-to-output step that makes it useful.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Follow a product beauty view with a close functional detail such as cargo loading or underwater foils.
try: For Tin workflow films, pair an overview screen with one enlarged input-to-output mechanism and a short label.
For a physical product launch, follow the same cargo box from loading to destination and reserve separate frames for verified specifications.
lessons.avoid: Letting attractive presentation imagery imply validated engineering or commercial performance.
lessons.open: Prototype status, technical performance, asset provenance, sound and exact motion remain unverified.
